---
title: "Study 06D: Moderate-sparsity SBayesRC annotation positive control"
description: "Matched one-replicate active-count contrast with frozen Study 08."
toc: true
toc-depth: 3
---

::: {.callout-important}
## Status

**STUDY10-R2 — genomic inference remains strong but annotation inference
remains weak.** The one pre-specified replicate is complete. Evidence remains
local and review-pending; no reference capsule is claimed.
:::

## Why?

Study 08 retained useful genomic inference but showed poor joint-alpha mixing
and chain-sensitive annotation priors in an extremely sparse architecture.
Study 10 asks whether substantially more non-null allocation events improve
annotation identification under otherwise matched conditions.

## Matched contrast

Both studies use 4,500 training samples, 500 validation samples, 35,000
markers, 35 blocks, the same annotation matrix and nonintercept alpha, the same
fixed-E CSR contract, and the same MCMC schedule. Expected active component
counts change from 90 / 54 / 36 to 500 / 300 / 200.

Total heritability remains 0.5. Individual active-SNP effects are therefore
smaller on average in Study 10, so the contrast does not isolate active count
perfectly.

## Methods and scope

The only methods are SBayesR, ordinary joint SBayesRC, and ordinary joint
SBayesRC-S. This is one targeted positive-control replicate—not an EM study,
factorial benchmark, grid, calibration study, or formal sparsity-power study.

## Frozen realization

Deterministic continuation-stick calibration produced intercepts -2.64152,
-0.32327, and -0.48572 and achieved expected counts 34,000 / 500 / 300 / 200.
The realized counts were 33,989 / 502 / 305 / 204: 1,011 active markers, or
2.889%. Genetic and residual variances were both 1 and realized heritability
was 0.5. Active markers had enriched-binary prevalence 0.824 versus 0.130 among
null markers, while the realized null-annotation mean among active markers was
approximately zero.

## Genomic inference

Beta correlations were 0.755 for SBayesR and 0.811 for both annotation
methods. Validation genetic-value correlations were 0.761, 0.814, and 0.813;
phenotype-prediction correlations were 0.528, 0.566, and 0.565. The lower
values than Study 08 are expected context for the more polygenic architecture
with smaller individual effects at fixed heritability. Annotation modeling did
not materially degrade genomic recovery relative to the matched SBayesR
baseline.

## Continuous annotation inference

Joint SBayesRC did not meet the registered continuous-annotation screen. Its
worst nonintercept alpha R-hat was 1.876, minimum bulk ESS 5.70, and minimum
tail ESS 12.53. Nonintercept alpha RMSE was 0.318 and correlation was 0.773.
Pooled active-prior truth correlation improved from 0.912 in Study 08 to 0.975,
and minimum chain-to-chain active-prior Pearson/Spearman improved from
0.514/0.190 to 0.805/0.581. Those are meaningful improvements, but they remain
well short of stable joint inference.

## Annotation selection

SBayesRC-S assigned PIP 1.000 to both `enriched_binary` and
`continuous_signal`, and 0.0079 to `null_annotation`. The signal PIPs were 1 in
every chain; null PIP ranged from 0.0005 to 0.0297. Thus the selection behavior
was low-PIP and chain-stable for the null annotation. Selection alpha itself
remained poorly mixed (worst nonintercept R-hat 1.675; minimum bulk ESS 6.37).
`pi_A` mixed well (R-hat 1.0004), while first-stick `tau2` remained weak
(R-hat 1.118; bulk ESS 21.1).

## Decision

The result is **STUDY10-R2** because continuous alpha and induced-prior chain
stability remain weak despite approximately 1,000 expected active markers.
This substantially weakens the hypothesis that Study 08's failure was mainly
caused by extreme scarcity of non-null events. It does not establish active
count as causally irrelevant: per-active effect sizes also changed at fixed
heritability. The strong SBayesRC-S separation shows that the moderate-sparsity
architecture did improve the selection endpoint.

The evidence is sufficiently clear to stop after this one targeted scenario.
No additional active-count level, replicate, prior change, or chain extension
is proposed.
